key_insight: In obstructive sleep apnea, the EEG-Respiratory Gap captures differences between EEG-derived and measured respiratory-event burden associated with long-term mortality beyond AHI.
clinical_relevance: These EEG-derived metrics may offer prognostic information beyond respiratory-event frequency, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Developed a deep-learning model to estimate AHI from a single EEG channel.
Calculated ΔAHIbrain to reflect EEG-derived AHI above or below expectations for measured AHI.
Estimated AHIbrain,event-free from epochs without scored respiratory events.
evidence_signal: Developed using 22,044 sleep recordings, the model correlated with measured AHI internally (r = 0.88) and across three external test sets (r = 0.50–0.62); both gap metrics were associated with all-cause and non-CVD mortality among participants initially free of CVD after adjustment for AHI and clinical risk factors.
watch_item: Lower external correlations raise generalizability concerns, and mortality associations do not establish causality or clinical benefit.
paper_title: The EEG-Respiratory Gap: a deep learning biomarker associated with long-term mortality in obstructive sleep apnea
